traceability.notes:
The JSDoc tag coexistence behavior described in docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md has not been implemented.
The current annotation parser (normalizeCommentLine + processCommentLine + collapseAnnotationValue) explicitly exhibits the problematic behavior called out in the story: when a traceability annotation like `@req REQ-OPTIMIZATION` is followed by another JSDoc tag line such as `@param {object} data`, the second line is treated as a continuation of the `@req` value. That combined value is then whitespace-collapsed into a single token like `REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data`, which fails validation and produces the kind of invalid requirement ID error described in Issue #3.
No logic exists to: - Detect generic JSDoc tags (`@word`) as boundaries, - Stop continuation when the next line starts with another JSDoc tag, - Or otherwise ensure proper termination of annotation values at tag boundaries.
Tests do not cover the coexistence scenarios (traceability tags interleaved with @param/@returns/@throws), nor is there any test suite labeled for Story 022.0 or its requirement IDs. Documentation for valid-annotation-format has not been updated to include examples or narrative about JSDoc tag coexistence.
Given the missing parser changes, absence of targeted tests, and lack of documentation updates, multiple acceptance criteria are not met: JSDoc tag detection as boundaries, correct continuation logic, prevention of false positives in mixed JSDoc blocks, and explicit documentation and tests for these combinations. The story is therefore not fully implemented.
